en: The Questions of Milinda:
The Chapter on Vessantara, Concerning the Question of Inference.

12. The Question on the Proximity of Nibbāna “Venerable Nāgasena, is there any location—in the eastern direction, the southern direction, the western direction, the northern direction, above, below, or across—where Nibbāna is present?
“There is no such location, Great King, in the eastern direction, the southern direction, the western direction, the northern direction, above, below, or across, where Nibbāna is present.”
“If, venerable Nāgasena, there is no place where Nibbāna is present, then surely Nibbāna does not exist?
And for those by whom that Nibbāna has been realized, their realization must also be false; I shall state the reason for this.
Venerable Nāgasena, just as on earth there is a field which is the source of grain, and a flower which is the source of fragrance...”
"There is a thicket of flowers, there is a tree of fruits, and there is a mine of jewels;
whoever desires whatever [of these] goes there and carries it away.
Even so, venerable Nāgasena, if Nibbāna exists, there must also be a place for the arising of that Nibbāna."

"It should indeed be desired, venerable Nāgasena; however, because there is no place from which Nibbāna arises, I say that Nibbāna does not exist, and for those by whom Nibbāna has been realized, their realization is also false.
"There is no place where Nibbāna is stored, Great King, yet this Nibbāna exists. One who practices rightly realizes Nibbāna through wise attention."
But just as, O Great King, there is such a thing as fire, yet it has no fixed place of abode, and one attains fire by rubbing together two pieces of wood;
even so, O Great King, there is Nibbāna, yet it has no fixed place of abode, and one who practices rightly realizes Nibbāna through wise attention.
Or again, O Great King, there are such things as the seven treasures.
That is to say:
the wheel-treasure, the elephant-treasure, the horse-treasure, the jewel-treasure, the woman-treasure, the householder-treasure, and the counselor-treasure.
There is no fixed place where these treasures reside; rather, for a kshatriya who practices rightly, those treasures come to him through the power of his right practice.
“In the same way, great king, Nibbāna exists, though it has no localized place; one who practices rightly realizes Nibbāna through wise attention.
“Venerable Nāgasena, let there be no localized place for Nibbāna; but is there that state, established in which one who practices rightly realizes Nibbāna?
“Yes, great king, there is that state, established in which one who practices rightly realizes Nibbāna.”
“But what, venerable sir, is that state, established in which one who practices rightly realizes Nibbāna?

“Virtue, great king, is that state. Established in virtue, attending wisely—whether in Sāketa, Cīnapaṭṭana, Alasanda, Nigumba, Kāsī, Kosala, Kaśmīra, Gandhāra, on a mountain peak, or even in the Brahma-world—one realizes Nibbāna.”
Wherever one may stand, if one practices rightly, one realizes Nibbāna. Great King,

it is just as any man with sight sees the sky, regardless of where he stands— whether in his own country, in Cīna, Vilāta, Alasanda, Nigumba, Kāsī, Kosala, Kaśmīra, Gandhāra, on a mountain peak, or even in the Brahma-world.

In the same way, Great King, one who is established in virtue and attends to things with wise attention realizes Nibbāna—whether standing in his own village, or indeed wherever he may be—provided he practices rightly.
Or again, Great King, just as in his own village... [and so forth].
“Just as there is an eastern direction for one standing anywhere whatsoever,
even so, Great King, for one established in virtue and attending wisely—
even in Sāvatthī itself… [and so on]… for one who has entered upon the right path and stands anywhere whatsoever, there is the realization of Nibbāna.”
“Excellent, venerable Nāgasena! You have taught Nibbāna; you have taught the realization of Nibbāna; the qualities of virtue have been fully explained;
right practice has been demonstrated; the banner of the Dhamma has been raised high; the guide of the Dhamma has been established;
the proper application of those who are well-directed is not in vain. Thus it is, O most excellent among the best of assemblies; I accept it as such.”
The twelfth question: On Being Close to Nibbāna.
The third chapter: The Vessantara Chapter.
In this chapter there are twelve questions.
